answers.ask: No visual theme was given beyond a grey baseplate prototype — should the finished map read as sci-fi, fantasy, or stylized toon?
answers.answer: Use a stylized toon prototype look: clean, colorful, highly readable shapes on the flat baseplate.

scene_prompt: Create a simple stylized-toon tower-defense map on a flat grey baseplate, using clean colorful, highly readable shapes. A straight path made of parts runs from an enemy spawn point at one end to a base at the opposite end. Arrange fixed agent placement slots at intervals along both sides of the path, with open space around them for clear visibility; the base is the path endpoint.
agent_notes: This is the Tower Defense preset stated almost line for line: a spawn mouth, one fixed route enemies are hard-coded to walk, flat slots flanking it for deploying agents, and a base at the end that is the health pool. Shape is lane-actor-track, whose P6 is structural and not negotiable — the lane has to be one continuous valid route with no ambiguous crossings or the waves break — so the track is generated first and the toon styling from the answers dressed onto it afterwards. I dropped the preset's choke-bottleneck because v1 explicitly asks for a straight path of parts on a flat baseplate and one enemy type, so a bunching pinch would be scope the prompt refused, and I kept the plateau build zones out for the same reason, which leaves the route flat. I read 'wave-survival' as the author's second name for tower defense rather than a second genre: nothing here is threat evasion by the player, the base takes the damage, and every option Survival would have contributed is already in Strategy's table. Enemies traverse the lane, so this is not a SET even though the player interacts by tapping slots.
